mainProgression.description: Classic rock chord progression with the familiar I-IV-vi-V movement that gives the verse its confident, driving feel. The C#m adds emotional depth before the dominant B chord pushes back to the tonic.

sectionProgressions.description: Guitar-driven intro establishing the bright E major tonality with Neil Giraldo's signature riff
Same progression as intro underneath Benatar's powerful verse delivery
Simplified three-chord anthem with the most fundamental rock progression, maximizing sing-along accessibility

sectionProgressions.progression: A - B - C#m - A - B - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - V - vi - IV - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: Building section that moves through the subdominant and dominant before resolving triumphantly to E major

harmonicFunction: E (I) - Bright, confident tonic establishing the anthemic major key
A (IV) - Subdominant providing harmonic motion and warmth
C#m (vi) - Relative minor adding a touch of tension and emotional depth
B (V) - Dominant chord driving resolution back to the tonic

techniques.name: Power Chord Anthem Strumming
techniques.description: Driving rhythm guitar using a mix of open chords and power chords with aggressive downstroke strumming that defines the anthemic arena rock sound

notes: E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (open E major) or E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (power chord)
A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (open A major) or A5: X-0-2-2-X-X (power chord)
C#m: X-4-6-6-5-4 (barre chord) or C#5: X-4-6-6-X-X (power chord)
B: X-2-4-4-4-2 (barre chord) or B5: X-2-4-4-X-X (power chord)
Mix of open chords in verse and power chords in chorus for dynamic range
sequence: Start with open E chord, strumming steady eighth notes
Transition to A with a slight accent on beat 1
Move to C#m barre chord (or power chord for easier version)
Hit B chord with emphasis, letting it ring into the next E
In chorus, switch to full power chord voicings for heavier sound
tips: Use mostly downstrokes for the driving, punchy feel
Add slight palm muting between chord changes for tightness
The transition from C#m to B is the trickiest - practice this change in isolation
Open E and A shapes sound fuller than power chord versions for the verse
details.progression: E - A - C#m - B (verse) / E - A - B (chorus)

techniques.name: Neil Giraldo Lead Fills
techniques.description: Melodic lead guitar fills between vocal phrases using the E major pentatonic scale, featuring double stops and sustain-heavy bends

notes: Lead fills primarily in E major pentatonic at the 9th and 12th positions
Double-stop sixths on the B and G strings are a signature move
Bends from G# to A (major 3rd to 4th) provide the vocal-like quality
Vibrato on sustained notes is wide and expressive
Fills are melodic and singable, not shred-oriented
sequence: Learn the E major pentatonic shape at the 9th fret
Practice the signature double-stop fill on B and G strings
Work on half-step and whole-step bends with accurate intonation
Add fills between vocal phrases in the verse sections
Build the solo gradually from melodic phrases to faster runs
tips: Giraldo's style emphasizes melody over speed - every note should sing
Use the neck pickup for warmer lead tones on fills
Wide vibrato is essential - practice shaking from the wrist, not the fingers
Listen to the vocal melody and make your fills complement it
details.progression: Lead fills over E - A - C#m - B progression

techniques.name: Barre Chord Transitions
techniques.description: Moving between open position chords and barre chords at the 2nd and 4th frets, a fundamental intermediate guitar skill showcased in this song

notes: C#m at 4th fret requires clean barre chord technique
B at 2nd fret barre chord shape (A-shape barre)
Quick transitions from open E/A shapes to barre chord positions
The key is minimizing hand movement between positions
Keeping the index finger ready for barre position during open chords
sequence: Practice C#m barre chord until it rings cleanly
Practice B barre chord with thumb behind the neck
Drill the transition: E (open) to C#m (4th fret barre)
Drill the transition: A (open) to B (2nd fret barre)
Chain all four chords together at increasing tempos
tips: Think of barre chords as movable open chord shapes
Keep your thumb behind the neck center for barre chord leverage
Start transitioning slowly - speed comes from accuracy, not force
If barre chords are too difficult, use power chord substitutions

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Neil Giraldo's signature guitar riff establishing the bright E major tonality with a melodic lead line over power chords
notes: Clean guitar riff with slight overdrive on the intro melody
The riff outlines the chord progression melodically
Second guitar enters with power chords on the repeat
Sets the confident, anthemic tone for the entire song

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Driving rhythm guitar supporting Pat Benatar's powerful verse vocal with the four-chord progression and lead fills between phrases
notes: Rhythm guitar locks in with steady eighth-note strumming
Lead guitar adds melodic fills between vocal phrases
Dynamics stay controlled, saving energy for the chorus
Clean-to-crunch tone with moderate overdrive

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The iconic singalong chorus simplified to three chords for maximum anthemic impact with full band intensity
notes: Full volume power chord strumming for anthem effect
The three-chord simplicity is part of the hook's brilliance
Emphasize the B chord with a harder strum before resolving to E
Both guitars play rhythm in unison for wall-of-sound effect

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Neil Giraldo's melodic guitar solo featuring bends, double stops, and E major pentatonic runs with singing sustain
notes: Solo is melodic and singable, built around the E major pentatonic scale
Features signature double-stop bends on the B and G strings
Wide vibrato on sustained notes is essential for the Giraldo sound
Builds from melodic phrases to faster runs before resolving

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Repeated chorus with building energy and lead guitar embellishments driving to the final E major resolution
notes: Repeated chorus progression with full band intensity
Lead guitar adds increasingly flashy fills over the rhythm
Build to the final climactic hit on E major
Song ends cleanly on a strong E major chord

guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for rhythm, neck humbucker for melodic lead fills

alternatives: Fender Twin Reverb with overdrive pedal

effects.distortion: Natural amp overdrive with slight boost for solos (MXR Distortion+ or similar)
effects.delay: Short delay (80-120ms) on lead parts for depth
effects.reverb: Moderate plate reverb for spacious arena sound
effects.other: No whammy bar needed. Wireless system optional for stage presence.

beginner.focus: Learn the open chord shapes and basic strumming pattern
steps: Master E and A open chord shapes with clean transitions
Learn a simplified C#m (using power chord X-4-6-6-X-X)
Learn a simplified B (using power chord X-2-4-4-X-X)
Practice the basic I-IV-vi-V progression at 80 BPM

intermediate.focus: Add full barre chords, proper strumming dynamics, and play at tempo
steps: Master C#m and B as full barre chords
Practice the strumming pattern with proper accents at 130 BPM
Add dynamic contrast between verse (moderate) and chorus (full)
Learn the basic melodic fills between vocal phrases

advanced.focus: Learn the guitar solo and add Neil Giraldo's signature lead embellishments
steps: Map out the E major pentatonic positions used in the solo
Learn the signature double-stop fills and bends
Practice the full solo at half speed, building to tempo
Combine rhythm and lead parts for a complete guitar performance
advanced.timeEstimate: 4-6 weeks for full performance with solo

commonMistakes: Struggling with the C#m barre chord - use power chord substitute until barre is solid
Playing verse and chorus at the same volume - dynamics are crucial
Rushing through the B to E transition at the end of the chorus
Over-distorting the tone - this song needs clear, defined crunch, not heavy gain
practiceRoutine: Warm up with E-A-B open chord transitions for 3 minutes
Practice C#m and B barre chords individually until they ring clean
Run through the verse progression (E-A-C#m-B) at 100 BPM for 5 minutes
Practice the chorus (E-A-B) with accented strumming for 5 minutes
Play through the complete song structure at gradually increasing tempo
focusAreas: Clean barre chord voicings at the 2nd and 4th frets
Dynamic control between verse restraint and chorus intensity
Tight rhythm guitar locked with the drum pattern
Smooth transitions between open and barre chord positions
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM with the full four-chord verse progression
Increase by 10 BPM per session until reaching 130 BPM
Practice chord changes landing precisely on beat 1
Use metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4 for rock backbeat feel
